quest.title: A Divergence Leading to Oneself
quest.description: The situation appears far worse than you previously imagined, with anomalies occurring in Irminsul and Nahida in a coma... It seems best to first leave Sumeru City with everyone and head for Caravan Ribat.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1425, Mora x62225, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act IX
chapter.title: As All Falls to Emptiness

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How is the Dendro Archon?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Her breathing is steady. I prepared some therapeutic incense for her, but it hasn't had much effect.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Her vitals are still very weak. Based on the information you've provided, I have a working hypothesis: Her condition is partly due to Irminsul's influence, and partly due to a physiological imbalance caused by the rapid depletion of her power.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Elemental energy usually flows through the body at a relatively constant rate. The body grows accustomed to this rhythm, so when it's thrown out of balance, physical symptoms will appear.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is this similar to the Ley Lines? Overloading and Withering both directly affect their vitality, potentially causing irreversible damage.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Correct. From a biological perspective, if you overexert yourself, you pay the price with your life. The Dendro Archon is not only drained of power, but her life force is at a critically low level.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Is there any way to restore her health?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I know the Ley Lines have strong self-healing abilities. As long as any blockages or pollutions are dealt with, they can quickly regain their vitality. But what about people... well, gods? What's their capacity for self-healing?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Before we think about that, there's a bigger predicament to resolve. Restoring the Dendro Archon's power requires us to heal Irminsul first — but that will be extremely difficult without the Dendro Archon's power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Paimon's already getting lost here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Tighnari and Cyno are discussing the current situation at pace. I have to concentrate hard to keep up.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: (Master Tighnari and Cyno look so serious... I've not heard Master speak in this tone for a long time.)

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Tighnari.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Master Naphis... Sages.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Tighnari! Haven't seen you in ages!

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: ...Have you gotten taller? Or did your ears get longer?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hopefully the former, Uncle Baladhuri.

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: Cyno, where's Professor Cyrus? I thought he'd be with you.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: He went out into the wild to investigate the situation. He said that the Irminsul anomaly will likely start to affect the real world soon.

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: He shouldn't be trotting around alone at his age... Which way did he go? I'll look for him later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Would someone mind introducing us?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Ah yes, of course. Allow me to do the honors.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: #I'm sure we're all familiar with {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They're the heroes who helped foil Azar's conspiracy and save Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: These gentlemen and I are the six current sages of the Akademiya. Baladhuri and I are part of the old guard, while the other four took office after Azar and his clique fell from power.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: We have Sage Alkindi of the Spantamad Darshan, Sage Firnas of Kshahrewar...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Rtawahist Sage, Shakir, and finally, Haravatat Sage, Rushd.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—Nice to meet you all!

choices.text: It's an honor.

response.speaker: Rushd
response.text: I've heard much about you. Delighted to finally meet you in person.

response.speaker: Shakir
response.text: Haha, you're younger than I imagined for someone with the power to stand up to fate itself. Thank you for lending your aid to Sumeru once more.

response.speaker: Baladhuri
response.text: Once we're on the other side of this, could we get a photo together? My daughter has a friend named Isak. He's always talking about you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! No true hero would deny a child their wish.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: Ahem, back to business. So, with the Dendro Archon currently in a coma, the people have taken temporary refuge at Caravan Ribat — but they cannot stay here forever.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: We need to come up with a plan as soon as possible. Firnas, any thoughts?

response.speaker: Firnas
response.text: Well, firstly, having reviewed the data, I'm inclined to agree with your assessment. This doesn't look like an attack on Irminsul from the outside. Rather, it resembles a malfunctioning machine, calculations going haywire and sparks flying.

response.speaker: Firnas
response.text: That being said, before we consider how to fix it, we need to understand precisely what has gone wrong. Furthermore, we somehow need to ascertain this without relying on the Dendro Archon's power.

response.speaker: Alkindi
response.text: We have no direct access to Irminsul. However, we might be able to gather the information we need from the Ley Lines. Study the branches to learn about the trunk, in other words.

response.speaker: Alkindi
response.text: (Wait... Is that what Cyrus is up to? No wonder he ran off to research in the wild... Curses. Always one step ahead of me, isn't he?)

response.speaker: Rushd
response.text: I heard that while in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, the Dendro Archon had to serve as the central information hub herself. This is a clear sign the situation within Irminsul might be far worse than we can imagine.

response.speaker: Rushd
response.text: Irminsul is vital not just to the safety of Sumeru, but to all of Teyvat. We must be the ones to bear responsibility for this world... To be on the safe side, I think we need to consider some backup plans.

response.speaker: Baladhuri
response.text: Are you saying we should consider a scenario in which Irminsul is completely destroyed?

response.speaker: Rushd
response.text: I'm merely pointing out that the possibility exists.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: You have a valid point. But until worse comes to worst, I believe we should focus our efforts on resolving the Irminsul anomaly and helping it recover.

response.speaker: Shakir
response.text: Collei, I understand that you were the first to foresee this crisis? If it's alright, I'd like to talk with you about it in more detail.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Of course! But even I don't know how I came to have that dream...

response.speaker: Firnas
response.text: If there are no signs of external damage, could it be a stress fracture? Metals tend to suffer from this issue with long-term use, and Irminsul has existed for centuries, after all...

response.speaker: Alkindi
response.text: It's possible, but surely a stress fracture would be more likely to cause a complete shut down rather than chaos...

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: Sages, General Mahamatra... Sorry to interrupt, but something has come up.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: What happened?

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: Some citizens didn't believe that Sumeru City was really in any danger. They slipped away and hid during the relocation, intending to return home.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: How many people are we talking?

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: About a dozen. Sekkura found them while on patrol, but they appeared to be suffering from psychosis... For whatever reason, they were trying to kill each other.

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: By the time we arrived, there were only two survivors. One was unconscious from their injuries, the other tried to attack us but was subdued.

response.speaker: Alkindi
response.text: Where did this happen?

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: Near Yasna Monument.

response.speaker: Baladhuri
response.text: ...That's not far from Caravan Ribat.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Master.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: I know. The Irminsul anomaly is beginning to have effects in the world. I didn't expect it to spread to Yasna Monument so soon... It almost feels like we're being chased relentlessly, with no time to catch our breath.

response.speaker: Rukh Shah
response.text: Sir Cyrus said the same thing. He sent me back to report in while he continues investigating.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I'll go join him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll come with you.

response.speaker: Alkindi
response.text: Count me in too. Don't let my age fool you, I can still fend for myself.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: Very well. Meanwhile, the rest of us will continue discussing our next steps.

response.speaker: Rushd
response.text: Get back soon.

response.speaker: Baladhuri
response.text: Take care of yourselves. It's getting dangerous out there.

choices.text: We'll be working together closely to resolve this crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Please, don't go any further. As you get closer to Sumeru City, there's no knowing what dangers you might encounter.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: So this is our mentally disturbed man?

dialogues.speaker: Tawfiq
dialogues.text: I'm going to gut you all! Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: Cyrus! You didn't even bring a single guard!? Do you think you're some sort of warrior?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It's fine. Come here and look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh... It's...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A Ley Line Blossom?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: That's right. Flowers that bloom from openings in the Ley Lines, indicating some sort of anomaly.

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: I don't believe I've ever seen a color like this before.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Did you discover it nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Not just here... Way over there too... They're everywhere! There's even more in that direction!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How did you ascertain the situation further ahead? Didn't you just say that we can't go beyond this point?

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Yes, this area is relatively safe so far, but if you continue forward, delusions will start afflicting your mind.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: However, some Vision-bearing mercenaries were able to maintain their sanity a little better. They're the ones who brought back news from further afield.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Cyno, do you remember the class I taught on dissecting Ley Line blossoms?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I do, Professor. I received full marks in that course.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Good. After all these years, it's time to put that knowledge into practice. There must be anomalous information hidden within these blossoms. Alkindi, I'll need your help as well.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Been a while since we worked on a project together, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Alkindi
dialogues.text: Sure has. Well, what are we waiting for? Let's get to work!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anything we can do to help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Nahida once said that Irminsul doesn't contain any information about me... So theoretically, I shouldn't be affected by such anomalies.)

choices.text: We'll head a little further out.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Will you need my help?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I should be fine.

response.speaker: Cyrus
response.text: Alright. Well, don't go too far. There's too many unknowns at this stage.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Let's regroup at Caravan Ribat later. Don't worry, if you don't show up, I'll come and find you.

choices.text: We'll see what else we can find.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Dark clouds gather in the sky, a sure sign that a storm is approaching.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Slowly but surely, the strange weather is spreading. The rainforest creatures must have sensed that something is wrong, because they're beginning to flee too.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We don't have much time left. Tighnari said that to help the Dendro Archon regain her power, we need to heal Irminsul, but healing Irminsul requires the Dendro Archon's power...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is there any way to solve this puzzle?)

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That should be the Heart of Oasis. All we need to do is light it with the Fire Seed and it'll restore Apep with elemental power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The damage it suffered internally will also slowly begin to heal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's it...!)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I use Apep's "Heart of Oasis," I might be able to help Nahida replenish her lost Dendro power without any need to rely on Irminsul!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? You thought of something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I know a way to save Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really!? Then let's get back and tell the others!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Phew. Glad to see you've returned safe and sound.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Any longer, and we would've gone out looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, well this is a nice surprise! Paimon sure feels better with everyone we know here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's great to see you all.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We've made some progress, so let's start by giving you and Paimon a quick update.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: By dissecting the Ley Line blossoms, we've been able to deduce that although Irminsul is experiencing an anomaly, it has not completely rejected access from the outside.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Dendro Archon has the power to connect to Irminsul, but there's also another way... I assume you recall the devices everyone was wearing when you first arrived in Sumeru?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Devices? Oh, wait! You mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Akasha terminals?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! It's been so long, Paimon almost forgot all about the Akasha. Wasn't it shut down, though?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yes, but although the system isn't currently operational, the technological infrastructure is all still there.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: And it turns out that a certain someone gets so bored at work that he's actually read through every single one of the instruction manuals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No prizes for guessing who that was.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: If praising others is that embarrassing for you, you can simply spare yourself the ordeal.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hmph. As much as it pains me to say anything nice about him, there's no denying his intelligence. He rarely forgets anything he's read.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The Akasha is exactly what Sumeru needs at this moment. Between us, we should have all the knowledge and expertise we need to get it up and running again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if I recall correctly, doesn't the Akasha need a Gnosis to function?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's exactly right. The Akasha relies on the Gnosis as a power source, and in its absence, we'll need to find an alternative. To tackle this problem, it looks like we'll be relocating once again.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Namely, to the Temple of Silence... Ring any bells?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: It's the only major institution in Sumeru dedicated to preserving the knowledge of King Deshret's civilization. You might find the answers you're looking for are hiding there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I agree, there's a good chance.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Master Naphis and the other sages have discussed it. As the chaos from Irminsul continues to spread, Caravan Ribat won't be a safe haven for much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We have to move into the desert next. The scholars and sages will head to the Temple of Silence, while the civilian population seeks refuge in Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: The Eremites will keep everyone safe during the journey, and Candace will be there to receive us at the village.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: This leaves us just one thing to worry about.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: She's very weak... We can't afford to wait until Irminsul is fixed. There has to be another way to help her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe, well luckily, {NICKNAME} had a eureka moment while we were out investigating.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: #Wow. Nice one, {NICKNAME}! Let's hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell everyone about the time you and Nahida saved Apep...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What say our Amurta experts?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Theoretically, it's feasible. From what you're saying, although elemental life and elemental energy have their differences, the Dendro Archon has explicitly stated that she can imitate the power of the former.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: In which case... as long as Apep is willing, she should be able to convert her own power into a form that the Archon can use.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It wouldn't be difficult for her at all. The only problem is convincing her to help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll find a way to persuade her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, even though she wasn't exactly friendly the last time we met, she didn't refuse to talk with us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once she realizes the danger that Nahida is in, surely she won't turn a blind eye to it. Uh... well, hopefully not?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Either way, we're not exactly spoiled for choice here.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hey, it's better than having no options at all!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I agree. Without Irminsul's aid, the legendary Dendro Dragon Apep may well be the only living thing in Sumeru who can help our Archon recover her power.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: There's no time to lose. I'll bring this proposal to Master right away. If he and the other sages agree, we'll split into three teams:

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #The academics will go to the Temple of Silence to look for a solution to the Akasha problem, the Eremites will escort the civilians safely to Aaru Village, and {NICKNAME} and Paimon will take the Dendro Archon to see Apep.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: There's still a long road ahead, and no knowing if we'll make it — but at least we have a direction now. I'll take it over floundering around in confusion.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If there are no objections, then let's proceed. But before we adjourn, I would like to leave you all with some parting words.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: "No matter the distance between us, there will always be an invisible force tying us together. May the bonds forged in the past shine bright like stars and open a new path before our feet."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh... Is that from King of Invokations?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: No. This one's from King of Invokations: The Sequel.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What's the difference?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The sequel's much cooler.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Couldn't agree more.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Well, it was very apropos. Once this is all over, I'll give everyone a copy of King of Invokations and the sequel to show my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Come on, let's get moving.

talks.objective: Inform the Grand Sage of the plan

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Tighnari has brought me up to speed. I approve of your plan of action.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: But we can't proceed with everything right away. The people need to rest. For many of them, this will be their first time in the desert, so we'll need to find additional personnel to help escort them.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: You two, please go on ahead with the Dendro Archon. Let's rendezvous at the Temple of Silence later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! We got this.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Words can't express my gratitude, so let me just say: I hope everything goes smoothly, for all of us. Goodbye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get going. If Paimon remembers correctly, the last time we saw Apep was in—

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... Could I borrow you guys for a moment? It'll only take a second!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Collei! What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Well... The thing is...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Master Tighnari once told me: "After you raise a problem, you should think about how to resolve it." But ever since I had that dream, I feel like I haven't been of any help at all.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I tried my best to keep up with the conversation, but there was so much new information, I couldn't take it all in. So I just wanted to ask... do you have any tips for me there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon knows exactly how you feel.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But fear not! Everything you need to know is right here in Paimon's Notes: Sumeru Chapter!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's got tons of info about all the things we've seen and heard on our adventures. Uh... Some parts are a little simplified, but hopefully it all makes sense!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You sure kept that one quiet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! You see? Being the greatest guide in Teyvat isn't just a fancy title. It takes a lot of hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't always understand the things you're talking about with other people. Whenever that happens, she notes down the confusing parts and goes over them in her own time.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: This is perfect! Could I borrow it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! Matter of fact, you can keep it if you want. Paimon has another copy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The spare copy was originally meant for {NICKNAME}. Paimon used to worry that one day, {M#he}{F#she} might not need a guide anymore, so she wanted to have a gift for him in case we ever parted ways...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it doesn't seem so necessary nowadays. We have so many more places to see together, one copy will be enough for both of us.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thank you so much! But still, these are your treasured memories... I think I'll make my own copy and then return the original to you.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Anyway, that was all — I won't keep you any longer. Have a safe trip! See you again soon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See ya!

choices.text: Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! Just ask Paimon whenever you need them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, time to bring Nahida to see Apep... Let's hope that old grouch is in a negotiating mood.

choices.text: Would I be allowed to borrow your notes too?

talks.objective: Take Nahida to search for Apep

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Alright. Well, don't go too far. There's too many unknowns at this stage.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Let's regroup at Caravan Ribat later. Don't worry, if you don't show up, I'll come and find you.

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: Hah. I had a feeling your kind might come calling.

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: The Ley Lines are in disarray. Something has gone wrong with Irminsul, yes?

choices.text: Nothing gets past you.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Even from a great distance away, I can sense that Sumeru is headed for destruction.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: You who took our home from us, prepare to watch as your own world is plunged into oblivion... Hahaha... Oh, how the cycle of history comes to a poetic conclusion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This isn't a joke, Apep. Nahida's in grave danger! Can you please help her?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Is she, now? Then, do explain: For what reason should I lend Buer my assistance?

choices.text: The safety of Sumeru depends on it.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Be not mistaken, the fate of Sumeru is of no concern to me. I am neither the god of this land, nor its guardian.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I may have given my tacit agreement as your kind built homes here and multiplied for generation upon generation... but that does not mean that I bear any responsibility for Sumeru.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Tiny Buer, puny humans... In my eyes, all of you are but intruders who followed in the wake of the Heavenly Principles. I am not obliged to be your savior.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Now that is a compelling reason.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: When Al-Ahmar plotted against me, and I was tortured by forbidden knowledge, it was Buer who saved me from agony.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: And though I regard with shame the pity of my enemies, to receive aid without repaying it would likewise tarnish a dragon's dignity.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Oh, tiny Buer, puny humans... Just this once, I shall deign to show you the true power of dragonkind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... it's happening again! We're gonna get sucked in!

choices.text: Hold onto me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Waahhhhh...

choices.text: We don't have the protection of the fire seed this time!
The very survival of the world could be at stake.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Hmph. The age of the dragons ended long ago... And the world that replaced it is under the dominion of the Heavenly Principles.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: In choosing not to side with your enemies when the Heavenly Principle's rules began to relax, I have been merciful enough...

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Do not forget that I have no love for this world you hold so dear.

choices.text: Because you owe a debt of gratitude, and this way you can repay it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Apep, if you truly despise gods and humans so much...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well... After the great humiliation of being helped by a god in the past, shouldn't you be jumping at this chance to balance the scales?

choices.text: I guess we can skip the explanation then...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (This is an awkward silence... Is silence a mandatory part of an audience with a dragon?)

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: It is done. The Heart of Oasis is supplying her with life force as we speak. It shall not be long before she recovers.

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: But I should warn you: Buer's existence is closely intertwined with Irminsul. Unless the issues plaguing it are resolved, she will never completely recover her former strength.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: Spare me your words of gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will giving your power to Nahida affect you in any way?

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: ...You may also spare me your feigned concern.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Ugh! Just like last time... It's impossible to have a normal conversation with this dragon!)

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: A dragon sovereign's power is far greater than you can imagine. While I was indeed weakened when the Heart of Oasis ran dry, providing Tiny Buer with a morsel of my life force shall have little consequence for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good to hear...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Just like Apep once said, the elemental lifeforms who merged with her have now been reborn.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The knowledge, memories, and emotions they once had are gone... They're brand new individuals now. And yet, for some reason, they seem drawn to Paimon and me.)

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: Ever held in high favor, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, hehe, well, y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Apep
dialogues.text: The compliment was sincere. Simply accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Come to think of it... I'm curious how Apep sensed the Ley Line anomaly from so far away, and immediately guessed that something was wrong with Irminsul.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Could she know something that we don't?)

choices.text: Apep...

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: ...I did once.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: That tree was not planted by the Heavenly Principles. Irminsul existed before they ever arrived in Teyvat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: There was a time when it belonged to Teyvat, to dragonkind.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Its appearance and function then differed greatly from today. The Ley Lines flowed with an abundance of a familiar, primitive form of elemental energy... You may know it as the power of the Light Realm.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: The Heavenly Principles usurped and refashioned Irminsul, made it serve humanity, and used it to anchor the fate of the world. Haha... Yet in the end, humanity has failed to protect it.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Heavenly Principles, god of gods... It makes me sick. The enmity between your kind and mine can never be bridged.

choices.text: Even so...

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: As things stand today, holding a grudge against you would serve no purpose.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: But there will come a day when we reclaim this world for ourselves. The opportunity will arise, no matter how long we must wait.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I can already sense that far away from here, the Hydro Dragon has wrested his authority from the hands of the usurpers.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Though we have yet to meet, I know that we are both preparing for our revenge day and night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It's probably best if we don't tell Apep that we're on such good terms with the Hydro Dragon...)

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: ...I hear a great disturbance out there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What is it?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Sandstorms come... The Jinn? Hmm, I see.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What happened?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Another calamity approaches. You both seem restless — let us part ways here.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Buer is safe with me. Once she has recovered, I shall return her to your side.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thanks again. Take care, alright?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: I told you already, I have no need of your feigned concern.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There she goes again...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We've done what we came here for. Time to check what's going on out there...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... N—Nahida? You're awake? Are you okay?

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Cease your interrogation. Yes, she awoke for a brief moment, but she has now lost consciousness again.

response.speaker: Apep
response.text: Take it. We shall talk more at another time.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "The statues of the gods hang inverted from the heavens, but one alone is unique among them."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "Its location is □□□□□□□. Remember, tell no one."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The moment I touched the key Nahida handed over, a mysterious piece of information appeared in my mind...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I don't know what it means, nor how to decipher it, but I will firmly commit it to memory.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This must be incredibly important information... I don't know why Nahida would keep it a secret from everyone, but it's probably best that I do the same for now.)

choices.text: You still agreed to help us.
Do you know much about Irminsul?

talks.objective: Return to the Temple of Silence
Return to the Temple of Silence

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There's no need for everyone to stay here. I'll protect the sages — the rest of you, return to Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Yes, Mahamatra Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno, what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You're back! How is the Dendro Archon?

choices.text: She's still with Apep, but she's recovering.

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: What a relief...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's with these sandstorms?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's the Jinn. Countless Jinn have stirred up violent sandstorms across the desert, blocking our path to the Temple of Silence.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Tighnari and Collei have returned to Aaru Village to help. The Jinn are being highly aggressive, so both the village and the merchant caravans require protection.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: It's just one thing after another... Where did all of them come from, anyway? In all my trips to the desert, I've never seen anything like this before.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: As I see it, the only possible candidate is Gurabad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gurabad?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Baladhuri could explain in more detail if he were here. All I know is a rumor I've heard about from previous trips to the desert — supposedly, a great number of dormant Jinn lie sealed beneath that city.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Jinn from Gurabad, huh...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A familiar figure comes to mind.)

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Gurabad is, for me, a fated land. I must therefore return back to this city, where my destiny awaits me still.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My master... I am sorry that I couldn't stay by your side for long, that I could not have more time to get familiar with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liloupar...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon and I should take a trip to Gurabad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. We once said goodbye to a friend there... Well, maybe not a "friend," exactly, but someone we met on the road, anyway. She was a strange bottle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we can find a way to wake her up, maybe she can help solve the situation in Gurabad.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: Well, be careful. You may find there's more than just the Jinn to worry about.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You mean, there are other dangers in Gurabad?

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: It's a sensible assumption to make. The moment we arrived in Caravan Ribat, the Irminsul anomaly started spreading in that direction. Now we've moved to the desert, and suddenly we're plagued by Jinn and sandstorms.

response.speaker: Alhaitham
response.text: To call it a coincidence would be a stretch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, we've gotten a lot stronger since our last stint in Sumeru!

response.speaker: Monster Roar
response.text: Raargh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! When did they show up!?

response.speaker: Naphis
response.text: It appears that the monsters native to the desert have been stirred by the Jinn's activity.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You should get going. We'll take care of things here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be careful.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You too.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Don't do anything too risky! You got it?

choices.text: Apep gave Nahida some of her own life force.

talks.objective: Go to the ruins of Gurabad
Break the seal on the Jinn
Enter Gurabad to learn about the situation
Find a way to enter the inner room
Plumb the depths of Gurabad's ruins
Plumb the depths of Gurabad's ruins

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The sandstorm's gone. The sun shines bright again.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: When I said that we'd meet again under a lovelier sun... This was exactly how I imagined it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, yay! Although honestly, Paimon would love to hang out with you more, even if the weather sucked!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That goes for me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, there shouldn't be any more Jinn breaking out, right? Are we okay to head back?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah. Let's all head to the Temple of Silence.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Sounds good. You can introduce us to your other friends.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Haha, another adventure begins. Lovely!

talks.objective: Defeat the enemy in your path
Destroy the device affecting the Jinn

dialogues.text: ...It seems my subordinates failed to stop you in your tracks.

dialogues.speaker: Balashov
dialogues.text: Apologies, Sir.
There is no need to apologize. You did well to hold your ground against such a powerful adversary for as long as you did... I must commend your courage and perseverance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're in charge here, huh? First the problems with Irminsul, now this mess in Gurabad... Are you the ones responsible for all this?
I'm afraid I cannot answer that.
Hehe... I assume you aren't naive enough to expect answers from an enemy?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Grr... This guy is so... so... snooty!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: However you wanna spin it, you're clearly involved in this somehow. So you can either start talking, or we'll have to make you talk!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Let's get him! ...{NICKNAME}? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Something seems unusual about him... Is he trying to provoke us? This feels like a trap...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Judging by the tents and supplies, there must be many more Fatui stationed here than the few we saw on the way in. So where are the rest?)
You're remarkably calm. Some would act more rashly upon finding the ringleader all alone, but you keep your cool... Even as your enemy, I must applaud you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you show yourself just to say that?
Is this you trying to take back control of the conversation? Unfortunately, I really don't have anything to say to you.
I am here merely to indulge my own curiosity... Your names are well known among the Fatui. Naturally, I wanted to observe you up close while I had the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't treat us like we're some kind of... exotic animals in a zoo!
Oh, I wouldn't dream of it. You seem rather predisposed to misunderstand me.
I'm quite aware that you are both heroes of great renown. You have resolved crises in many nations and won countless allies along the way...
I've been following your adventures with great admiration. My only regret is that the trajectory of your journey conflicts with our goals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean "admiration"? Sorry, but that sounds pretty weird coming from you...
I don't see why. We may happen to occupy opposing sides, but there is no cause for deep-seated enmity between us. To respect one's enemy is to respect oneself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, now that you're observing us up close, what do you see?
I've observed as keenly as I can. Yet while I endeavor to understand, your true strength remains a mystery to me.
Violence is not my area of expertise either... So, you see, I would much rather converse with you like this than determine a victor with the edge of a blade.
Besides, I've heard that even three moons in the sky failed to eclipse your brilliance. I know better than to bite off more than I can chew.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Three moons...!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So you have a connection with the Harbinger, "The Doctor"?
Well deduced. Our commander, Dottore, died in Nod-Krai. But there are things that do not end with his departure. We must...
Ah, look at me. I almost divulged more than I should have.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you after? Revenge for Dottore? Or are you plotting something else...

I've said quite enough, I believe. There's no point in continuing this conversation... Except to say, I've noticed that you seem to know your way around here quite well. A repeated visitor to Gurabad, are we?
I'll take that as a yes. Then I'm sure you'll have heard the story of this place... The "Mother of the Jinn," Liloupar, and the tragic tale of her vengeance that spanned three generations.
It was right here that Liloupar once helped the wise to ascend to the throne. But from that moment on, every king who sat upon it was corrupted by power.
These degenerate rulers lost control over their nation, and with it, the right to occupy that exalted seat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you trying to say?
I once admired you for your adventures. That is the earnest truth. But it appears to me that your journey serves ultimately to uphold the rules of this world.
Are these rules truly just? Does the Heavenly Principles rule with wisdom, or folly? And how can we be sure that The Seven, who wield authority over the world, will not be corrupted?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you seriously think you're gonna convince us of anything?
Convince you? Haha. I'm sure my commander already tried that. Why would I waste my breath doing the same?
If a few words from a stranger were enough to make someone completely change their stance, it would only prove that they never had a firm will to begin with.
I am merely stating my position so that we might understand each other better. One's enemy in the present may not necessarily be an enemy for life.
As for what game I'm playing here... I'm simply buying some time. But now, I must bid you farewell.
It was a wise decision not to attack me immediately. Since you did not fall for my ambush, I will now have to ask those in hiding to reveal themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Sedova
dialogues.text: Leave this to us, Sir.
#Very well. I trust you to do what is necessary. Stall {M#him}{F#her} while I execute the next step of the plan.
Sumeru City, Irminsul...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, stop right there! Don't you dare leave without explaining yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Kolomiyets
dialogues.text: All units, stop them! Protect the commander!

talks.objective: Defeat the Fatui in your way

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Found him! Over here!
You're very persistent.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you! Stop running, and explain yourself! What're you trying to—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's this..?
Relax. A small trap like this won't be enough to hold you.
The sandstorms from Gurabad will die down soon enough, but this small window of time was all we needed to launch the next phase of our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So there was more than one ambush... I shouldn't have let my guard down!)
Don't be discouraged. I knew that someone would come here eventually, so I planned ahead.
Where to chat with you, which door to exit from, even which mechanism to wait by for you... I thought through every detail.
You, meanwhile, know nothing of who I am. So far, you've only heard my voice — and for all you know, it may not even be real.
But not to worry. This is only our first meeting. It shan't be our last.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just answer me one last question. Why do you continue to follow Dottore? He has conducted countless cruel experiments... even on his subordinates.
"Follow" isn't quite the right word. Let's just say, even those you see as villains have their friends, even if they aren't the most sincere of friendships.
When any set of rules is established, there will be those who benefit and those who lose out. People will do anything to justify what they have gained or escape from the hardship imposed upon them.

Neither he nor I are tolerated by the rules of this world. We were both searching for a new order... Our ideas of the final form that should take may have differed, but our journeys took a shared path.
#Goodbye, {NICKNAME} and Paimon. I wish you a timely escape... albeit not too soon. I will need a little more time to prepare, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Come baaaack!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, this dark wall... We've seen these on our adventures before! It swallows people up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sorry... She shouldn't have jumped the gun...

choices.text: It's not your fault, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Hmph, he may have fooled us this time, but we'll get him back!

choices.text: Let's just focus on getting out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Cyno and his team are guarding the north. We'll take this side.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: There are so many Jinn... We can't let them get into Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't fret! I am well prepared for this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Huh? So you have a solution?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Perhaps you're unaware that I have a trusty Jinni partner of my own, Plumpy. If I send her to negotiate with the others, this whole thing will resolved before you can say "Mora."

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Off you go, Plumpy!

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: C'mon! What's the holdup?

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub.

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: 100,000 Mora, final offer!

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub-blub!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ah, so she's a hired partner.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hired partners are reliable too! Plumpy here is a highly skilled negotiator. You'll see — just a few words from her, and...

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Plumpy...!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't you Jinn have any respect for the rules!? This was supposed to be a negotiation! How dare you treat my messenger like this!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You wanna play rough? Two can play at that game!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Aaaah!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Looks like it's up to us now. Be careful, Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yes, Master!

talks.objective: Defeat the Jinn causing the disturbance
Follow the guidance of the mysterious voice

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: There's too many of them!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I can't believe I used 12 rare items in one battle! Ugh... I shudder to think how this is going to affect this month's accounts... The sight of that glaring deficit might be more than my poor heart can take...

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Tighnari, how's the situation on your end?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We held the line, though it was a close call. But it looks like they're preparing for another attack... Has something happened?

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: They've breached our defenses in the south! The Jinn are pouring in! We're moving the villagers to the north as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We're hemmed in... This is getting precarious. Our margin for error just got a lot smaller.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: That's why we wanted to confirm your status. We need to consider our next move carefully...

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Bad news! Another line of defense has been breached!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei, go with them and assess the situation. Dori and I will hold the line here.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But, Master...! Even with three of us, we barely managed to—

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This is not a discussion, Collei. Don't worry about us — she clearly still has plenty of tricks left up her sleeve.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Wait, you can't pin all your hopes on me!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Oh, great... I've almost run out of the things I brought with me, and the rest is back at the caravan. I should be able to hold out for a little longer, but still...)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master...
Need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What is it, Collei?
If things continue like this, it won't be long before Aaru Village is overrun by Jinn, and the sandstorms are sure to follow in their wake. I do have a plan, but I can't guarantee it will work.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I don't care. Whoever you are... Please, just help us!
The only one who can help is you. I am merely here to guide you along the correct path.
"I am a spirit created at the beginning, I am a flickering illusion, I am the shimmering light that flows from the eyes of the creator."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: What do you mean?
It doesn't matter, you don't need to understand it. Just repeat after me, one line at a time.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Watch out, Jinn incoming!
"I am a spirit created at the beginning."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Phew... Here goes nothing! "I am a spirit created at the beginning"...

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub...?
"I am a flickering illusion."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "I am a flickering illusion"...

dialogues.speaker: Plumpy
dialogues.text: Blub!!!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Plumpy? I've never seen you so agitated before.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: That's... But how do you...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Do you know what Collei is reciting?
"I am the shimmering light that flows from the eyes of the creator."

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "I am the shimmering light that flows from the eyes of the creator"...

dialogues.speaker: Jinn
dialogues.text: Roar...

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: It's a song composed by the Goddess of Flowers. But very few records of it remain, even in historical texts. All we have is a few fragments.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Is Collei an avid historian?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Not to my knowledge.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: The Jinn have actually quieted down. Although... no, it's more than that. It looks like they're showing... submission.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: Hmm... Clearly, the songs left by the Goddess of Flowers have a soothing effect on them. At the very least, they're much calmer now.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Really? Let me try...

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: "I am a spirit created at the beginning"...

dialogues.speaker: Jinn
dialogues.text: Raargh!!

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Eek! Stay away! I'll stop, I'll stop!

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: It seems like the song only works when Collei recites it. But why?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Collei...

talks.objective: Try to break through the trap

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hyah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any luck?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The only way out of here is by brute force. But too much force, and the entire ruins might collapse.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The mechanism is right outside. Maybe there's a way to...)
Heh. When I heard that loud rumbling in the distance, I thought the shifting sands had bust open the gates to some ancient treasure vault... Turns out it was just you guys.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, that sounds like—

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It's been a long while... Did you miss me?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep-beep, beep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht! Benben!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Let's save the catching up for later — first, I gotta get you guys out of there.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This should be the right mechanism... Benben, can you handle it?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: There we go.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's leave this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, those Fatui sure made themselves scarce. It's like they were never here.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The Fatui? They came to the desert again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup. No idea what they're planning this time... They were being very coy about it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How have you been, Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, since we last met, I've started my own band of mercs. We've actually made quite a name for ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh yeah — on a slightly different note, I have some good news.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I finally took care of Masseira. Not much to write home about... It was just another day. Found his hideout, dragged him out of his cozy little bed.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: He tried to talk me into seeing his point of view, as usual. But I'm way past that by now. There was nothing he could say to save his life.

choices.text: So the Masseira chapter has finally come to a close.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: What about you guys? Bet you'd forgotten all about me and Benben, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course not! We're super-duper best friends!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly recount the events of your recent travels to Jeht...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Wow. Sounds like I should make time to visit some other nations, too. Anyway, what brings you to Gurabad?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Paimon almost forgot! We're here to look for Liloupar.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, that bottle?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, that bottle?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. We need her power to calm the Jinn and stop the sandstorms.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Here's hoping we actually manage to find her, after all the trouble we've been through... Surely, with everything that's been going on in Gurabad, she must've woken up, right? Only one way to find out...

choices.text: Remember to wipe the blood off your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Liloupar!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: What a long dream that was... It's been a while, my master.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Oh, and you're here too, little wildcat. The four of us, back together again. Imagine that!

choices.text: How've you been?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: After we last parted ways, I merged with the land beneath Gurabad to suppress the dark calamity stirring in the depths.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It rekindled the flame of vengeance within the Jinn, depriving Gurabad of any hope of peace.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I fought against it for a long, long time — until one day, I sensed a change in a foreign land to the west. Suddenly, the pitch-black Abyss fell silent.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (A foreign land to the west... Could she mean Natlan? Gurabad isn't far from there. Did the Abyssal presence beneath this city fall silent when we defeated Gosoythoth?)

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Once satisfied that that dark power could no longer bewitch the Jinn, I too fell into a deep slumber, from which I have only now awoken.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Why have you returned to Gurabad, my master? And why is my sand-swept homeland in disarray once more?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Basically, Sumeru's in danger and a lot of our friends are affected. Some bad guys messed around with Irminsul, and now they've released the Jinn in here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We managed to chase off the culprits, but we have no idea how to seal this place back up and stop the sandstorms.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Child's play. I shall quell the Jinn and scatter the storms.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you, Liloupar.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: No need to thank me, my master. I have granted many wishes in my time, and this was the most trivial of them all.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The sandstorm's gone. The sun shines bright again.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: When I said that we'd meet again under a lovelier sun... This was exactly how I imagined it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, yay! Although honestly, Paimon would love to hang out with you more, even if the weather sucked!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That goes for me too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Well, there shouldn't be any more Jinn breaking out, right? Are we okay to head back?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah. Let's all head to the Temple of Silence.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Sounds good. You can introduce us to your other friends.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Haha, another adventure begins. Lovely!

choices.text: I hope this wasn't a rude awakening?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: In truth, it was at first. I was none too pleased when those miscreants barged in... But it did give me the chance to reunite with you, dear master, so I shall overlook their folly.

talks.objective: Quell the sandstorm started by the Jinn
Quell the sandstorm started by the Jinn

dialogues.speaker: Shakir
dialogues.text: Don't be nervous, Collei. I just wanted to ask, have you ever had similar dreams to this one before?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Umm... Similar how?

dialogues.speaker: Shakir
dialogues.text: Dreams so vivid, they seem real. Filled with strange or dangerous things that you cannot explain.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Lemme think... There was one time. I don't remember it very clearly, but I saw...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Fire.

dialogues.speaker: Shakir
dialogues.text: Fire?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah. I wish I could give you more details, but all I remember is fire everywhere. From the sky to the ground, everything was burning... The heat was unbearable, and ashes were blowing in the wind...

dialogues.speaker: Shakir
dialogues.text: I doubt this dream was a mere coincidence. Perhaps it was some kind of prophecy? And yet, you've never studied astrology... I'm at a loss to explain it.

dialogues.speaker: Baladhuri
dialogues.text: I thought we'd be safer once we got to Caravan Ribat...

dialogues.speaker: Rushd
dialogues.text: If the Irminsul anomaly's sphere of influence continues to expand, our only option will be to move into the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Rushd
dialogues.text: To Aaru Village? We should check if they can accommodate so many people.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: Essential supplies will also become an issue. We were only able to relocate here so quickly because Caravan Ribat is well stocked.

dialogues.speaker: Firnas
dialogues.text: If we move to the desert, we'll need to carefully calculate how much food and water to bring...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Thank you for everything, Tighnari...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me — I'm fine. But if you don't mind me saying so, Master, you're looking a little nervous yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: I only just got appointed as Grand Sage, and now this happens... It's quite overwhelming.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Looking back now, I don't think I handled the situation with Azar very well at all. Yes, I protested, but I went about it the wrong way. Instead of helping, I just ended up getting locked away.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Now that I'm The Grand Sage, I have to be responsible for everyone's lives... including the dozen or so who fled to Yasna Monument. I can't help but blame myself for their deaths.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's only natural that you want to do the best job you can. But Master, we both know perfection is impossible.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: You're right. ...We may well be heading into the desert before long. Feeling up to it?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: We left in such a hurry that I didn't bring any sun lotion. But I'm sure I can make some from local ingredients here. That was a big part of my graduation thesis, after all. Still remember?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Of course, like it was yesterday. I remember asking you if you'd like to stay and teach, but you turned me down without a moment's consideration...

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Anyone else would fight tooth and nail for the chance to research by my side, but you couldn't get out the door fast enough. Weren't you afraid I'd hold up your thesis and stop you from graduating?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If you'd pulled a move like that, I would've reported you to the matra right away.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: You wouldn't give me a second chance? What about the bond between mentor and student?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No, Master. I would not sit by and watch you go astray.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Very good. Then I taught you well.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So, um... Can I assume that this period of time away won't count as part of the rental period? Maybe we should deduct it from next month's payment?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Sure.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Great... Wait, why are you suddenly being so reasonable? What's the catch?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm always reasonable with rental payments. Like the time I refused to let you use that wine you brought home as collateral.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That was a perfectly fair request and you know it! Everyone runs low on funds now and then, don't they? And that bottle of wine wasn't cheap. You ought to be thanking me.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Anyway, Sumeru City should be empty by now, right? With no one at home, I've been worried about security...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Worried about burglars? What would they steal? That new scroll you bought?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah! I'd almost forgotten about that. Ugh, I only went and hung it up in the most conspicuous spot in the house... If anyone breaks in, it'll be the first thing they see!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Well, no one but you gave it a second look while it was on display in the shop. I doubt anyone would go out of their way to steal it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You say that, but what if there's a thief out there who shares my aesthetic tastes?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Then you can only hope he shares your taste in expensive wine as well. Always worth having some collateral.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hat Guy!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nothing, you just looked like you were lost in thought there... Do you have any ideas about what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: From what I know about Irminsul, the system doesn't break down that easily.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I don't have the faintest idea who could have done this. ...Actually, one name did cross my mind, but... Hmph, he's already dead.

dialogues.speaker: Zakariya
dialogues.text: Take this medicine and get some rest. Long journeys are fatiguing at the best of times, and it's taken its toll on your health. Please focus on recovering for the next couple of days...

dialogues.speaker: Aryadeva
dialogues.text: Got it. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: Keep your eyes peeled! It's down to us to maintain order at this time.

dialogues.speaker: Nidal
dialogues.text: This is a direct command from the Mahamata. Everyone, stay vigilant. We cannot allow bad actors to take advantage of the chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, here's a thought... If we brought Neuvillette along, do you think he could help us persuade Apep to help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Actually, never mind. In Apep's eyes, Neuvillette's probably one of those dragons who's "grown too close to humankind"... They might end up fighting for all we know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where the heck are we? Did she just dump us in the middle of nowhere!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no, Paimon remembers now! The Temple of Silence is over that way. C'mon, let's go find the others!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Jinn are swarming out of Gurabad... Looks like Alhaitham was right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get inside and see what's going on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They just keep coming... How many of these things are there!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll never take them all out... Let's just head further inside for now.

dialogues.speaker: Sedova
dialogues.text: Target spotted! All units, at the ready!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Fatui!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They must be using this place as a stronghold! Are they the ones behind all this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fighting Jinn with one hand and Fatui with the other... This is pure chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Careful! They're back again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This mechanism looks different from the last time we were here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we want to go further inside, we have to figure out how to open this door...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Success! Nice one, {NICKNAME}! Let's keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This hunk of junk's gone kaput! Now we can finally—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you hear that? He mentioned Sumeru City and Irminsul... He definitely knows something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We can't let him get away! Get rid of these pesky soldiers, quick!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You know... this reminds me of when you first arrived in Avidya Forest.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You were trying to help a child retrieve a lost toy when you stumbled upon Spinocrocodile territory by mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Yeah, I remember... Our first time fighting side by side.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Fighting side by side? I seem to recall swooping in to rescue you with a team of forest rangers...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Uhh, hehe... Please stop...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... She should be around here somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: If things continue like this, it won't be long before Aaru Village is overrun by Jinn, and the sandstorms are sure to follow in their wake.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I do have a plan, but I can't guarantee it will work.
